The route is a low-angle gneiss slab; a regional article calls it a 350-metre, 10-pitch route, while the pitch list (about 56 m each, 562 m total) is distance along the slab, not vertical height. 10 pitches in both fields agree; length_m is the route's height.

Mountain Project lists 10 pitches (1600 ft) and its description gives the 4+6+2 breakdown; the six 4th-class pitches are described as ideal for simulclimbing, so they are not separate roped pitches in the count. No source gives a different total.

Parks Canada's descent guide and trip accounts describe two-bolt stations about 25 m apart; a 25 m rappel is exactly what a 50 m rope doubled provides, so 'spaced for a 50 m rope' and '25 m rappels' agree.
